displayName: loop-sessions: a source token expires within two weeks

conditions.displayName: nearest source token expiry below 14 days for 1 h

documentation.content:
A live source token expires in under fourteen days. Every token carries a mandatory expiry of at most 180 days, and a platform whose token lapses stops posting without a sound (the beacon and the hook drop their 401), so the rotation has to finish before the date. `REDUCE_MIN` reports one incident for the nearest expiry, and the other expiring tokens hide behind it: read every token, not the one the incident names.

`gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="loop-sessions" AND jsonPayload.message="skill token summary"' --freshness=10m --format='value(jsonPayload.platform,jsonPayload.environment,jsonPayload.source_token_id,jsonPayload.expires_in_days,jsonPayload.last_used_minutes_ago,jsonPayload.rate_limit_per_min)'` grouped by `source_token_id`. For each token under 14 days: mint its successor for the same platform and environment (`POST /v1/admin/source-tokens`, expiries staggered 150 to 180 days so they never share a week), add a GSM version of `loop-sessions-skill-usage-token-<platform>-<environment>`, push it to the vendor, wait for the old row's `last_used_minutes_ago` to climb or 24 h, set the old limit to 0 for a day, revoke. A token that reads `expires_in_days` 0 was hand-inserted with no expiry: revoke it and mint properly.

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-source-tokens
